summary: Mery Cecconi is an Indology scholar. She studied as a doctoral candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter Bisschop (attested 2026).
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer, and served as Vice President of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Michael Aris (1946–1999) was a scholar of Tibetology and history. He studied under David Snellgrove at SOAS and held posts at Oxford, including St Antony's College and Wolfson College, as well as Harvard University.
Michael Balk specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held a post at the Berlin State Library (attested 1991).

Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) studied at Cambridge and under Ernst Gombrich. He held academic posts at the Warburg Institute, Courtauld Institute of Art, the University of Oxford, Cornell University, and the University of California, Berkeley.
Michael Bernays (1834–1897) studied at the University of Bonn and Heidelberg University. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).
Michael C. Shapiro is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a Professor at the University of Washington from circa 1970 to 2013, later becoming Professor Emeritus of Hindi.

Michael Carrithers is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Wesleyan University and the University of Oxford, and served as Professor of Anthropology at Durham University, along with posts at Oxford and LSE.

Michael Comans is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong, as well as under Dayananda Saraswati and R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and taught at the University of Sydney.

Michael Como is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Bernard Faure, Carl Bielefeldt, and Kuo-liang Wang, and is the Tōshū Fukami Associate Professor of Shinto Studies at Columbia University.

Michael Eido Luetchford is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied electronic engineering at the University of Bradford, studied under traditional teacher Gudo Wafu Nishijima, and founded Windbell Publications.

Michael Friedrich is a sinologist who completed his PhD at the University of Munich. He served on the faculty at the University of Munich and was a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1994 to 2021.
Michael G. Morony is a historian and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at UC Berkeley and UCLA, becoming a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1974.

Michael Hahn (1941–2014) was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Wilhelm Rau at the University of Marburg. He held professorships at the University of Bonn and the University of Marburg.
Michael Harack is a scholar in religious studies and sinology. He earned his Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2007).
Michael Hookham is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa in 1965 and founded the Longchen Foundation.

Michael Hutt is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his BA and doctorate at the University of London. He held several posts at SOAS, including Head of the South Asia Department and Associate Dean.
Michael J. Tetreault is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He earned his Master of Arts at San Diego State University under supervisor Sandra A. Wawrytko (attested 2011).

Michael J. Walsh is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at the University of Cape Town and the University of California, Santa Barbara, where he completed his doctorate under William F. Powell.
